lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala lun Israil inan Tuhan, "Kai pangeh nenganau' sala'. Do' Tuhan nganau' anun-anun luk pianMu kuan kai. Iamo' muit nekai aco sini.”
english: But the Israeli people said to Yahweh, “Truly we have sinned. Punish us in whatever way you wish to, but please rescue us now!”

lun_bawang: Idi lun mula' idi lun rayeh lun Giliad nengitun arangdeh sebuleng, "Idée luk miak mangun ku lun nguyut amée' pebunu' nelun Amon ineh? Idi ieh teh miak mangun ku lun nguyut amung lun luk tudo déei' Giliad."
english: The Israeli leaders said, “Who will lead our soldiers to attack the Ammon people-group? The one who will lead us will become the leader of all us who live in this Gilead region.”

lun_bawang: Idi awan tu Giliad pana' inan tuda'-tuda' anak deléei. Kareb anak awan tuneh pangeh rayeh, idi ideh nengecuk ni Yepta buro, kebaladeh, "Na iko miak ngalap babpat dengan lun bang ruma' taman kai. Ngaceku iko anak ratnan decur baken.”
english: Gilead’s wife gave birth to several sons. When they grew up, they forced Jephthah to leave home, saying to him, “You are the son of a prostitute, not the son of our mother. So when our father dies, you will not receive any of his property.”

lun_bawang: Kebaladeh neneh, "Do' iko amée' mangun ku lun nguyut nekai, pad kai miak pebunu' nelun Amon ineh.”
english: They said to him, “Come with us and lead our army, and help us to fight against the men from the Ammon people-group!”

lun_bawang: Iamo' Yepta nengor baladeh, "Na ui kelupan dat muyuh negku, ngaceku muyuh nengecuk negku buro rat bang ruma' tamanku. Amée' ngudeh teh muyuh negku, kareb muyuh inan susa'?”
english: But Jephthah replied, “You hated me RHQ previously! You forced me to leave my father’s house! So why are you coming to me now, asking me to help you when you are experiencing trouble?”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi'deh neneh, "Inan peh kai amée' ngalap namu nekini, ngaceku kai pian namu maya' nekai amée' pebunu' nelun Amon. Idi iko miak mangun ku lun nguyut amung-amung lun Giliad.”
english: The leaders from Gilead replied, “Yes, we are having trouble, and that is the reason that we have come to you now. If you come with us and help us to fight against the Ammon people-group, after we defeat them, we will appoint you to be the leader of all us people in the  Gilead region.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Yepta nedeh, "Kudeng muyuh ngalap negku lemubed idi amée' pebunu' nelun Amon, idi kudeng Tuhan marée tueh negku, ui miak mangun ku lun rayeh muyuh.”
english: Jephthah replied, “If I go back to Gilead with you to fight against the Ammon people-group, and if Yahweh helps us to defeat them, will you truly appoint me to be your leader?”

lun_bawang: Idi kebaladeh neneh, "Kai miak nganau' mepad kudeng balamu. Tuhan mo' luk miak nier netau.”
english: They replied, “Yahweh is listening to everything that we say. So he will punish us  if we do not do everything that you tell us to do.”

lun_bawang: Idi Yepta nengecuk nelun duken amée' inan raca' lun Amon pad ngitun neneh, "Anun inanmu museh nekai? Ngudehkée iko semuet bang bawangku?”
english: Jephthah sent some messengers to the king of the Ammon people-group. They asked the king, “What have we done to make you angry, with the result  that your army is coming to fight against the people in our land?”

lun_bawang: pad marée kali', "Kudeng ini bala Yepta: Lun Israil na nengaro tana' lun Moab idi tana' lun Amon pana.
english: They said to him, “This is what Jephthah says: ‘It is not true  that we Israelis took the land from the Moab people-group and the Ammon people-group.

lun_bawang: Idi Yepta nepejani' inan Tuhan, kebalaneh, "Kudeng Iko marée tueh negku rat nelun Amon,
english: There Jephthah made a solemn promise to Yahweh. He said, “If you will enable my army to defeat IDM the Ammon people-group,

lun_bawang: Iamo' ieh nemutuh inan tamanneh, "Ini luk pituenku namu. Nima' negku amée' nangi' luun pegkung dengan lun rurumku dueh bulan kinioneh, ngaceku ui matée na awan.”
english: Then she also said, “But allow me to do one thing. ◄First/before you do what you promised►, allow me to go up into the hilly area and wander around for two months. Since I will never be married and have children, allow me and my friends to go and cry together.”

lun_bawang: Idi tamanneh nengecuk neneh amée' dueh bulan kinioneh. Idi ieh inée' dengan amung rurumneh idi nangi' luun pegkung, ngaceku ieh matée na awan.
english: Jephthah replied, “All right, you may go.” So she left for two months. She and her friends stayed in the hills and they cried for her because she would never be married.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Yepta nedeh, "Ui dengan pupuku nepekedaluh dengan lun Amon. Idi pangeh ui nenawar nemuyuh. Iamo' na muyuh inée' muit negku rat nedeh.
english: Jephthah replied, “The Ammon people-group were oppressing us greatly. When we were prepared to start to attack them, I requested you to come and help us, but you refused. My men and I defeated the Ammon people-group, but you did not help us.

lun_bawang: Idi Yepta nengamung amung lun Giliad luk deléei idi nemunu' nelun Epraim, idi nengelaya' nedeh. Ngaceku lun Epraim nepebala, "Muyuh lun Giliad luk bang bawang Epraim idi Manasée pangeh neburo rat Epraim.”
english: Then Jephthah summoned the men of the Gilead region to fight against the men of the tribe of Ephraim. The men of the tribe of Ephraim said, “You men from the  Gilead region are men who deserted us. Long ago you left us and moved to the area between our tribe and the tribe of Manasseh.” Because of their saying that, the men of the Gilead region attacked the men of the tribe of Ephraim.

lun_bawang: Idi lun Giliad nengabang gitan Abpa' Yarden, pad lun Epraim na miak guta. Idi kareb lun Epraim luk buro mutuh guta, idi lun Giliad ngitun nedeh, "Iko lun Epraimkée?" Kudeng ideh mala, "Na",
english: The men of Gilead captured that ◄ford/place where people can walk across► at the Jordan River to go to the land where the tribe of Ephraim live. Whenever one of the soldiers from the tribe of Ephraim came to the ford to try to escape, he would say, “Let me cross the river.” Then the men of Gilead would ask him, “Are you from the tribe of Ephraim?” If he said “No,”

lun_bawang: Idi Melaikat Tuhan nesilagan inan awanneh, kebalaNeh, "Iko na anak. Iamo' na mio teh iko miak mali', idi nenganak aceh anak deléei.
english: One day, Yahweh appeared to Manoah’s wife in the form of an angel, and said to her, “Even though you have not been able to give birth to any children until now, you will soon become pregnant and give birth to a son.

lun_bawang: Idi Manua nesembayang inan Tuhan, kesembayangneh, "O Tuhan, do' nima' Lemulun luk icuk Allah ineh amée' nekai dueh teh, idi mada' nekai dueh anun luk miak ruen kai dueh kuan anak ineh kareb awanku nenganak neneh.”
english: Then Manoah prayed to Yahweh, saying, “O Yahweh, I plead with you, allow that prophet whom you sent to us to come again, and teach us how we should raise the boy who will be born to us.”

lun_bawang: Idi ieh petacu nupun inée' inan awanneh, kebalaneh, "Miket amée' nier Lemulun luk nesilagan negku atun di. Idi Ieh peh.”
english: So she quickly ran and said to her husband, “The man who appeared to me a few days ago has come back again!”

lun_bawang: Manua inée' maya' awanneh. Idi kareb Manua nepapu' Neneh, idi ieh nengitun, "Iko nepegayam inan awan kidi?" Kebala Melaikat ineh, "Mo, Ui idi.”
english: Manoah ran back with his wife, and asked, “Are you the man who talked with my wife a few days ago?” He replied, “Yes, I am.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Manua, "Kudeng apeh! Kareb luk pangeh bilaMu ineh mangun, anun luk ruen anak ineh? Anun kekamenneh?”
english: Manoah asked him, “When what you promised occurs and my wife gives birth to a son, what rules must he obey, and what work will he do when he grows up?”

lun_bawang: Idi Melaikat Tuhan nengor balaneh, "Do' awanmu nginita amung luk bida'Ku neneh.
english: Yahweh replied, “Your wife must obey all the instructions I gave her.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Manua inan Melaikat Tuhan, "Kai dueh sikal ngimet Namu, pad kai dueh ngeret aceh anak améek kuanMu.”
english: Then Manoah said, “Please stay here until we can kill and cook a young goat for you.”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Melaikat neneh, "Kudeng tudo tu pana', Ui na miak kuman luk kenenmu. Iamo' kudeng iko pian nganau' luk kuanKu, ngeseb ineh mangun ku aceh barée kuan Tuhan." Idi na Manua kali' Neneh Melaikat Tuhan.
english: Yahweh replied, “I will stay here, but I will not eat anything. However, you may kill an animal and sacrifice it as a burned offering to Yahweh.” (Manoah did not realize that the man he thought was an angel was really Yahweh.)

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Manua inan Melaikat Tuhan, "Mada' ngadanMu nekai dueh, pelée kai dueh miak ngubur Namu, kareb luk bilaMu ineh mangun?”
english: Then Manoah asked him, “What is your name? When what you have promised happens, we want to honor you.”

lun_bawang: Idi Melaikat Tuhan nengitun neneh, "Ngudeh iko pian kali' ngadanKu? Ieh ineh luk inalum.”
english: Yahweh replied, “◄Why do you ask me my name?/You should not ask me my name.► RHQ It is ◄wonderful/it cannot be understood►.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Manua inan awanneh, "Kali' rungen kiteh matée ngaceku kiteh pangeh nenier Allah!”
english: So he said, “Now we will die, because we have seen God!”

lun_bawang: Idi ieh nuli' idi nemada' taman-tinanneh, kebalaneh, "Déei' Timna ui nepapu' seburur decur lun Pilistin. Do' medueh ngalap neneh ku awanku.”
english: When he returned home, he told his mother and father, “I saw a young Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want you to get her for me so I can marry her.”

lun_bawang: Idi kudeng muyuh na kali' ilungneh na miak na muyuh marée teluh ngepulu' kuyu' luk meputeng idi teluh ngepulu' kuyu' luk mebuyor negku." Idi kebaladeh neneh, "Mala balée' midi pedingeren kai.”
english: But if you cannot tell me the meaning, you must each give me a linen robe and an extra set of clothes.” They replied, “All right. Tell us your riddle.”

lun_bawang: Kebalaneh, "Luk ngita' nengeruat luk kenen, luk metueh nengeruat luk mepaci'." Idi bang teluh aco nateh ideh kali' ilungneh.
english: So he said, “From the thing that eats came something to eat; out of something strong came something sweet.” But for three days they could not tell him the meaning of the riddle.

lun_bawang: Idi kareb aco luk keapat idi ideh nekidi inan awan Samson, "Do' iko ngubuk awanmu, pad ieh mada' nekai ilung balée' ineh. Kudeng na, kai ngeseb namu dengan ruma' tamanmu. Kian, medueh nenawar nekai pian ngalap binaweh kai lek?”
english: On the fourth day, they said to Samson’s bride, “Ask your husband to tell you the meaning of the riddle. If you do not do that, we will burn down your father’s house, with you inside it! Did you invite us here only to make us poor by forcing us to buy a lot of clothes for your husband?”

lun_bawang: Muci ratnan ineh idi Samson inée' ngikak awanneh kareb ngeranih. Idi ieh nenguit aceh anak améek, idi kebalaneh kuan ibanneh, "Ui pian amée' bang takep awanku." Iamo' ibanneh na nemarée neneh semuet.
english: During the time that they harvested wheat, Samson took a young goat to Timnah as a present for his wife. He planned to sleep with EUP his wife, but her father would not let him go into her room.

lun_bawang: Keburi'neh ni Samson, "Ui ngerawée iko museh neneh. Ngaceku ineh ui nemarée neneh kuan lun rurummu. Iamo' kinanakneh luk isuut do' taga rat neneh. Do' ieh lapenmu ku libalneh.”
english: He said to Samson, “I really thought that you hated her. So I gave her to the man who had been your best man at the wedding, and she married him. But look, her younger sister is RHQ more beautiful than she is. You can marry her!”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi' Samson, "Sekua' ini ui na mesala' kudeng ui ngua' dat lun Pilistin.”
english: Samson replied, “No! And this time I have a right to get revenge on you Philistines!”

lun_bawang: Idi lun Pilistin nengitun, "Idéekée nenganau' ini?" Idi kebaladeh, "Ieh ineh Samson, ngaceku ibanneh, lun Timna ineh pangeh nemarée awanneh kuan lun rurumneh." Ngaceku ineh lun Pilistin inée' ngeseb ruma' taman decur ineh idi nengeseb decur ineh teh.
english: The Philistines asked, “Who did this?” Someone told them, “Samson did it. He married a woman from Timnah, but then his father-in-law gave her to the man who was Samson’s best man at the wedding, and she married him.” So the Philistines went to Timnah and got the woman and her father, and burned them to death.

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Samson nedeh, "Kudeng inikée kekamen muyuh? Kali' rungen ui na ugka' kudeng ui na nengua' kuan muyuh.”
english: Samson found out about that, and he said to them, “Because you have done this, I will not stop until I get revenge on you!”

lun_bawang: Idi lun Yahuda nengitun nedeh, "Ngudeh muyuh munu' nekai?" Keburi'deh, "Kai amée' ngalap ni Samson idi ngedereh neneh, mepad kudeng ieh nengedereh nekai.”
english: The men there asked the Philistines, “Why have you attacked us?” The Philistines replied, “We have come to capture Samson. We have come to get revenge on him for what he did to us.”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi'deh neneh, "Kai inée' tungée', pian ngaling namu idi marée namu nelun Pilistin." Idi Samson nengor baladeh, "Pejani' negku idi pad muyuh na ngatée negku.”
english: But the men from Judah said to him, “We have come to tie you up and put you in the hands of the Philistines.” Samson said, “All right, but promise me that you yourselves will not kill me!”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi'deh, "Na kai ngatée namu. Iamo' kai pian ngaling namu mo' idi marée namu nedeh." Idi ideh nengabet neneh ku dueh nuper luk mebaruh, idi nenginat neneh rat bang lubang batu ineh idi nenguit neneh.
english: They replied, “We will just tie you up and take you to the Philistines. We will not kill you.” So they tied him with two new ropes, and led him away from the cave.

lun_bawang: Pangeh ineh idi Samson nemenani, "Ku tulang ada keladai ui nengatée meribu lemulun, Ku tulang ada keladai ui nengamung butung pebuun- pebuun.”
english: Then Samson wrote this poem: “With the jawbone of a donkey I have made them like a heap of dead donkeys. With the jawbone of a donkey I killed 1,000 men.”

lun_bawang: Idi Samson meparing. Ngaceku ineh ieh nengitang nawar Tuhan Allah, kebalaneh, "Iko pangeh nemarée tueh negku. Idi nekini ui léelée matée ku paring, idi miak kamen lun Pilistin luk na sinunat ineh.”
english: Then Samson was very thirsty, so he called out to Yahweh, “You have given me strength to win a great victory. So now must I die because of being thirsty, with the result that those heathen Philistines will take away my body and mutilate it?”

lun_bawang: Idi lun Gasa nekali' Samson idi bang bawangdeh. Idi ideh nengelibut bawang idi nengabang neneh kedangan-kedangan ineh munung tanga' bawang ineh. Iamo' ideh tudo kedangan-kedangan, keburi'deh, "Kareb pekak uka-uka kali' rungen tau ngatée neneh.”
english: People soon found out that Samson was there, so the men of Gaza gathered together at the city gate and waited all night. They said to themselves, “When it dawns tomorrow morning, we will kill him when he tries to leave the city.”

lun_bawang: Idi ngaceku ineh Delila nengitun ni Samson, "Mada' negku anun punmu pelaba tueh, idi anun luk miak ku ngaling namu, pad iko melaya'.”
english: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me what makes you so strong, and tell me how someone can subdue you and tie you up.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Samson, "Kudeng lun ngabet negku ku tudu' nuper luk mebaruh, ieh ineh luk na pikai, kali' rungen ui melaya', idi mangun mepad kudeng lun baken.”
english: Samson said, “If someone ties me with seven new bowstrings, ones that are not dry yet, I will become as weak as other men.”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi' Delila ni Samson, "Ngudeh iko nguto negku, idi mebalih negku. Mada' negku anun luk miak ku ngaling namu.”
english: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have deceived me and lied to me! Now tell me the truth, how someone can tie you up securely.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Samson neneh, "Kudeng ui kalingen picet-picet ku kalat luk mebaruh luk na nekungabet, kali' rungen ui melaya' mepad kudeng lun baken.
english: Samson replied, “If someone ties me with new ropes, ones that have never been used, I will be as weak as other men.”

lun_bawang: Idi Delila nengalap aceh kalat luk mebaruh, idi nengaling neneh ku ineh. Keburi' Delila, "O Samson, lun Pilistin macing amée' ngakem namu!" Idi lun luk ngabang ineh tudo bang takepneh selipa. Idi Samson nemutut kalat ineh ratnan penguanneh mepad kudeng gitian.
english: So again, she told the Philistine leaders, and they came and hid in the room as they had done before. And again, while Samson was sleeping, she took the new ropes and tied him up with them. Then she called out, “Samson! The Philistines have come to capture you!” But Samson snapped the ropes on his arms as easily as if they were threads.

lun_bawang: Kareb ieh rudap idi Delila nengebaruh abpukneh dengan pu ineh. Idi ieh nemicet neneh. Keburi' Delila, "O Samson, lun Pilistin macing amée' ngakem namu!" Idi petacu ieh netumui idi nenginat abpukneh ratnan iad tebaruh ineh.
english: and she tightened them with the pin. Then she called out, “Samson! The Philistines have come to capture you!” But Samson woke up and pulled out the pin, and pulled his hair from the threads on the loom.

lun_bawang: Idi keburi' Delila neneh, "Ngudeh iko megéei' mala iko mawa negku, iamo' iko mebalih? Iko pangeh mebalih negku teluh kua', idi nateh iko nemada' negku anun punmu metueh.”
english: Then Delilah said to him, “How can you say that you love me when you do not tell me the truth about yourself? You have deceived me three times, and you still have not told me what really makes you so strong!”

lun_bawang: Idi Delila nengitang, "O Samson, lun Pilistin macing amée' ngakem namu!" Idi ieh petacu nekulat. Idi keterawéeneh, "Ui miak mepuit mepad kudeng atun." Iamo' na ieh kali' Tuhan nenecan neneh.
english: Then after she tied him up, she called out, “Samson! The Philistines have come to capture you!” He woke up and thought, “I will do as I did before. I will shake these ropes off myself and be free!” But he did not realize that Yahweh had left him.

lun_bawang: Idi lun rayeh lun Pilistin nepamung pian marée aceh barée luk rayeh kuan Dagon akangdeh ineh dengan mawang niat. Idi ideh nemenani, "Akang tau pangeh nemarée tueh netau ratnan bunu' tau Samson!”
english: Several months later the Philistine leaders celebrated a big festival. During the festival they offered sacrifices to their god Dagon. They praised him, saying, “Our god has enabled us to defeat our great enemy Samson!”

lun_bawang: Kareb lun mula' ineh nenier neneh idi ideh nemenani ngubur akangdeh, kebaladeh, "Akang tau pangeh nemarée tueh netau, ratnan bunu' tau luk pangeh nengedat bawang tau, idi luk pangeh nengatée tuda'-tuda' burur arang tau!”
english: And when the other people saw Samson, they also praised their god Dagon, saying, “Samson ruined our crops and killed many of our people, but our god has put our enemy into our hands. Our god helped us to capture the one who has killed so many of us!”

lun_bawang: Idi kareb ideh marot, kebaladeh, "Nawar ni Samson amée' tungée', pad tau situnga neneh!" Idi ideh nenguit ni Samson remuat rat bang tutup. Idi ideh nesitunga neneh. Idi ideh nenganau' neneh tuped arang diri ruma' ineh.
english: By that time the people were half-drunk. They shouted, “Bring Samson out of the prison! Bring him here so that he can entertain us!” So they brought Samson from the prison and made fun of him. Then they made him stand in the center of the temple. They made him stand between the two pillars that held up the roof.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Samson inan anak deléei luk nguyut neneh, "Nguit negku amée' ngakem diri ruma' ini, ngaceku ui pian pusad luun ineh.”
english: Samson said to the servant who was leading him by his hand, “Place my hands against the two pillars. I want to rest against them.”

lun_bawang: Idi Samson nesembayang, kesembayangneh, "O Tuhan Allah, do' ngerawée negku, idi ngetueh negku sekua' ini mo', O Allahku, pad ui miak ngua' kuan lun Pilistin ku ideh nenakul matehku.”
english: Then Samson prayed, saying, “Yahweh, my Lord, think about me again! Please give me strength one more time, so that I may get revenge on the Philistines for gouging out my eyes!”

lun_bawang: Idi Mika nengitun neneh, "Rat iapeh iko?" Idi ieh nengor balaneh, "Ui ini seburur lun Liwi rat Baitlahim luk bang tana' Yahuda. Ui nakap bawang inanku tebawang.”
english: Micah asked him, “Where are you from?” He replied, “I come from Bethlehem. I am from the tribe of Levi, and I am looking for a place to live and work as a priest.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Mika neneh, "Do' tudo denganku, idi mangun ku lun mada' negku idi ku imam. Idi ui marée kuanmu pulu' balad pirak bang selak, dengan ayung luk petap, idi akan teh.”
english: Micah said to him, “Stay with me, and you can become like a father to counsel me, and be my priest. Each year I will give to you ten pieces of silver and some new clothes. And I will provide food for you.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Mika, "Nekini ui kali' Tuhan miak ngeperuan negku, ngaceku inan lun Liwi mangun ku imamku."
english: Then Micah said, “Now I know that Yahweh will do good things for me, because I have a man from the tribe of Levi to be my priest.”

lun_bawang: Idi ieh nengor baladeh, "Ui nepejani' ni Mika. Ui mangun ku imamneh, idi ieh mayar tabparku.”
english: He told them the things that Micah had done for him. And he said, “Micah ◄has hired me/is paying me to work for him►, and I have become his priest.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebaladeh neneh, "Do' iko ngitun Allah, pelée kai kali' kudeng kai inan peruan bang lawée kai ini.”
english: So they said to him, “Please ask God if we will succeed in what we are trying to do on this journey.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala imam ineh, "Na luk ku rapang muyuh. Ngaceku Tuhan matar nemuyuh bang lawée muyuh ini.”
english: The young man replied, “Things will go well for you. Yahweh will go with you on this journey.”

lun_bawang: Kareb ideh luk limeh burur ineh nelemubed inée' bawang Sora idi Estaul, idi pupudeh nengitun nedeh, "Anunkée luk sinier muyuh déei'?”
english: When those five men returned to Zorah and Eshtaol, their relatives asked them “What did you find out?”

lun_bawang: Idi ideh nengor baladeh, "Do' tau amée' munu' nedeh. Kai pangeh nenier tana' ineh pelaba do'neh. Anun ulek tudo ieni mo'-mo'? Miket! Nalan idi ngalap bawang ineh.
english: They replied, “We have found some land, and it is very good. We should go and attack the people who live there. Why are you staying here and doing nothing RHQ? Do not wait any longer! We should go immediately and take possession of that land!

lun_bawang: Litad ideh numak ruma' Mika idi nengalap amung akang ineh, idi imam ineh nengitun nedeh, "Anun luk ruen muyuh ni?”
english: When the priest saw them bringing out the idols and the sacred vest and the statue, he said to them, “What are you doing?”

lun_bawang: idi ideh nengitang nedeh. Idi lun Dan nelumi idi nengitun ni Mika, "Ngudeh muyuh pelaba ula'? Anun susa' muyuh?”
english: They shouted at them. The men of the tribe of Dan turned around and said to Micah, “What is the problem? Why have you gathered these men to pursue us?”

lun_bawang: Kebala Mika, "Muyuh ngalap amung akangku luk inau'ku ineh idi imamku pana' idi petacu nalan. Anun luk ketecan negku peh? Ngudeh muyuh mala, 'Anun susa?' “
english: Micah shouted, “You took the silver idols that were made for me! You also took my priest! I do not have anything left RHQ! So why do you ask me, ‘What is the problem?’”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala lun Dan, "Meluun do' iko na pebala anun-anun, pad kai na megateh niat idi munu' namu, pad iko na matée dengan amung uang tetek ruma'mu.”
english: The men from the tribe of Dan replied, “You should not shout loudly like that! One of our angry men might attack you and kill you and your family!”

lun_bawang: Idi pekak aco luk keapat, idi didueh netumui uka-uka, idi gugkang. Idi kebala taman decur ineh inan ibanneh, "Do' iko kuman atun idi teh medueh nalan.”
english: On the fourth day, they all got up early in the morning. The man from the tribe of Levi was preparing to leave, but the woman’s father said to him, “Eat something before you go.”

lun_bawang: Idi taman decur ineh idi ibanneh netudo. Idi didueh pana' nekuman idi ngirup. Idi kebala taman decur ineh kuan ibanneh, "Do' tudo aco sini teh, pad tau do' ria'.”
english: So the two men sat down to eat and drink together. Then the woman’s father said to him, “Please stay another night. Relax/Rest and have a joyful time.”

lun_bawang: Idi aco luk kelimeh pekak uka-uka, ieh netumui pian nalan. Iamo' kebala ibanneh, "Do' kuman atun. Idi napeh medueh miak nalan." Idi ibanneh nekuman denganneh.
english: On the fifth day, the man got up early and prepared to leave. But the woman’s father said to him again, “Have something to eat. Wait until this afternoon, and then leave.” So the two men ate together.

lun_bawang: Kareb ideh malée macing Yebus, idi aco pana' malée macep. Idi keburi' demulun inan tuanneh, "Do' tau rudap bang bawang ini.”
english: Late in the afternoon, they came near to Jebus. The servant said to his master, “We should stop in this city where the Jebus people-group live, and stay here tonight.”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala tuanneh neneh, "Tau na miak rudap bang bawang ini, ngaceku ini baken bawang lun Israil. Do' tau petacu amée' Gibia.
english: But his master said, “No, it would not be good for us to stay here where foreign people live. There are no Israeli people here. We will go on to Gibeah city.”

lun_bawang: Tau miak ngiuk sesuut teh idi rudap déei' Gibia kian Rama lek.”
english: He said to his servant, “Let’s go. It is not far to Gibeah. We can go there, or we can go a bit further to Ramah. We can stay in one of those two cities tonight.”

lun_bawang: Idi lun mengered ineh miti nedeh lun sakai ku ideh tudo luun natad di. Idi ieh nengitun nedeh, "Rat iapeh muyuh ni? Amée' iapeh muyuh?”
english: He realized that the man from the tribe of Levi was only traveling and did not have a home in that city. So he asked the man, “Where have you come from? And where are you going?”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala lun mengered ineh, "Do' muyuh amée' ruma'ku. Ui miak ngasa' nemuyuh. Ngaceku na do' muyuh rudap luun natad ini.”
english: The old man said, “I wish that things will go well for you, but I would like to provide what you need. Do not stay here in the square tonight.”

lun_bawang: Idi lun mengered ineh neremuat idi nepebala nedeh, "O kinanakku, aleg muyuh nganau' luk dat. Deléei ini sakaiku.
english: The old man went outside and said to them, “Friends, I will not do that. That would be a very evil thing. This man is a guest in my house. You should not do such a terrible/disgraceful/shameful thing!

lun_bawang: Idi kebala deléei ineh neneh, "Tumui! Nalan tau!" Iamo' na balaneh. Idi ieh nenganau' butungneh luun keted keladaineh, idi nenalan.
english: He said to her, “Get up! Let’s go!” But she did not answer, because she had died. He put her body on the donkey and traveled to his home.

lun_bawang: Idi lun pupu Beniamin nekali' bala amung lun Israil pangeh nenalan inée' Mispa. Idi kareb lun Israil nacing Mispa, idi ideh nengitun, "Mada' nekai kudeng apeh kekamen luk dat ini pangeh nangun?”
english: The people of the tribe of Benjamin heard that the other Israelis had gone up to Mizpah, but none of the men from their tribe went to the meeting there. The Israelis who had come to Mizpah asked about the evil thing that had happened.

lun_bawang: Idi lun Liwi, awan decur luk pangeh pinatée nengor baladeh, "Ui idi apidku inée' déei' bawang Gibia luk bang babpat Beniamin sikal rudap déei'.
english: So the husband of the woman who had been killed replied, “My slave wife and I came to Gibeah city, wanting to stay there that night.

lun_bawang: Idi amung lun Israil ineh netuped idi nepebala, "Na tu-tu tau muli', do' luk tudo bang lepo, idi luk bang ruma' pana'.
english: All the people stood up, and in unison said, “None of us will go home! Not one of us will return to his house!

lun_bawang: Idi amung pupu lun Israil ineh nengecuk tuda'-tuda' lun duken amée' anid- anid ruma' bang bawang pupu Beniamin, kebaladeh, "Kudeng apeh kekamen luk dat luk pangeh inau' muyuh?
english: Then the Israeli men sent messengers throughout the tribe of Benjamin. They demanded, “Do you realize that some of your men have done a very evil thing?

lun_bawang: Idi lun Israil inée' sembayang déei' Baitel. Idi ideh nengitun Allah, kebaladeh, "Pupu sapeh amée' munu' nelun pupu Beniamin atun?" Idi Tuhan nengor baladeh, "Pupu Yahuda atun.”
english: Those other Israelis went up to Bethel and asked God, “Which tribe should be the first to attack the men from the tribe of Benjamin?” Yahweh answered, “The men from the tribe of Judah should go first.”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi' lun Beniamin, "Ideh pangeh nelaya' mepad kudeng luk atun teh!" Iamo' kebala lun Israil, "Do' tau buro idi nayan nedeh rat bang bawangdeh pad macing dalan rayeh.”
english: Then while the men of Gibeah were running out of the city toward them, the other 10,000 Israelis came out from the places where they had been hiding, west of Gibeah. They were men who had come from all parts of Israel. There was a very big battle. But the men of the tribe of Benjamin did not know that they were about to suffer a disastrous defeat.

lun_bawang: idi lun Israil miak lemubed. Idi bang kareb ineh lun Beniamin pangeh nengatée teluh ngepelu' burur lun Israil, keterawéedeh, ideh miak ngelaya' nedeh mepad kudeng atun teh.
english: They surrounded some of the men of the tribe of Benjamin, and pursued the others to the area east of Gibeah.

lun_bawang: Idi lun Israil pangeh nepejani' inan Tuhan déei' Mispa, kebaladeh, "Kai na miak marée anak decur kai lapen lun Beniamin.”
english: When the Israeli men gathered at Mizpah before the battle started, they vowed, “None of us will ever allow one of our daughters to marry any man from the tribe of Benjamin!”

lun_bawang: kebaladeh, "O Tuhan Allah lun Israil. Ngudeh inan luk mangun kudeng ini kuan kai? Ngudeh sebuleng pupu lun Israil na idi?”
english: They kept saying, “Yahweh, God of us Israeli people, it is as though one of the tribes of us Israelis does not exist any more! ◄Why has this happened to us?/It is terrible that this has happened to us!►” RHQ

lun_bawang: Iamo' lun Israil méei' kuan kinanakdeh lun Beniamin. Kebaladeh, "Bang aco sini sebuleng pupu lun Israil na idi.
english: The Israelis felt sorry for their fellow Israelis from the tribe of Benjamin. They said, “Today one of our Israeli tribes ◄has disappeared/no longer exists►.

lun_bawang: Idi ideh nepitun, "Idéekée rat arang amung pupu lun Israil na nacing inan Tuhan déei' Mispa?" Idi ideh nekali' seburur pana' nateh luk nacing rat Yabis luk déei' Giliad ineh netebubpun dengandeh déei' su luk inandeh nelupo.
english: Then one of them asked, “What group from any of the tribes of Israel did not send any men here to Mizpah?”

lun_bawang: Idi amungdeh luk tebubpun ineh nengecuk 12,000 lun luk mesangit amée' ngatée amung lun bang bawang Yabis, perapu decur idi anak, keburi'deh,
english: So all the Israelis decided to send 12,000 very good soldiers to Jabesh-Gilead to kill the people there with their swords, even to kill the married women and children.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala lun rayeh-rayehdeh, "Na luk idi decur rat pupu Beniamin peh. Kudeng apeh tau miak marée awan kuandeh luk ketecan.
english: The Israeli leaders said, “We have killed all the married women of the tribe of Benjamin. Where can we get women to be wives of the men who are still alive?

lun_bawang: Tau na miak nala' sebuleng pupu tau. Do' tau nakap dalan pad pupu Beniamin miak amée' mula'.
english: These men must have wives to give birth to children, in order that their families will continue. If that does not happen, all the people of one of the tribes of Israel will die.

lun_bawang: Idi ideh nekidi nelun Beniamin, kebaladeh, "Amée' muyuh sigapung bang kabun-kabun anggur,
english: So the Israeli leaders told the men of the tribe of Benjamin, “When it is the time for that festival, go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards.

lun_bawang: Kareb ideh arang dalan Naomi nekidi inan ibanneh, "Do' medueh muli' amé' tudo dengan tinan medueh. Idi Tuhan ngedengan nemedueh, mepad kudeng medueh pangeh nengedengan negku idi nedidueh luk naté ineh.
english: Then as the three of them were walking, Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Each of you should turn around and go back to your mother’s home. You treated your husbands kindly before they died, and you have treated me kindly.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala didueh neneh, "Ara' kai dueh lemubed. Iamo' kai dueh pian amé' maya' namu amé' inan pupumu'.”
english: They each said, “No, we want to go with you as you return to your relatives.”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Naomi, "Lemubed mo' medueh iban. Ngudeh medueh pian amé' maya' negku? Na anakku luk ngalap nemedueh peh.
english: But Naomi said, “No, my daughters, return home. ◄It will not do any good for you to come with me!/What good will it do for you to come with me?► RHQ Do you think I will get married again and have more sons who could become your husbands?

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Naomi inan ibanneh Rut, "Siruh, seruaimu pangeh nuli' iné' matun pupuneh idi akangneh. Do' iko pana' muli' maya' seruaimu.”
english: Naomi said to her, “Look! Your sister-in-law is going back to her relatives and to her gods! Go back with her!”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Rut, "Aleg ngesaad negku necan namu idi mebpeng negku na amé' maya' namu. Ngaceku iapeh-iapeh suetmu, ui maya' namu. Idi iapeh- iapeh inanmu tudo, ieneh teh inanku tudo. Idi pupumu, ineh teh pupuku. Idi Allahmu, ineh teh Allahku.
english: But Ruth replied, “No! Don’t urge me to leave you! I want to go with you. Where you go, I will go. Where you stay, I will stay. Your relatives will be my relatives, and the God you worship will be the God I worship.

lun_bawang: Idi didueh nenalan pad macing déi' Baitlahim. Kareb didueh nacing bawang Baitlahim amung lun bang bawang ineh negagap. Kebala dawa' decur, "Ini Naomiké?”
english: So the two women continued walking until they came to Bethlehem. When they arrived there, everyone in town was excited to see them. The women of the town exclaimed, “◄Can this be Naomi?/It is difficult to believe that this is Naomi!►” RHQ

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Naomi nedeh, "Aleg neten negku Naomi. Ilung Naomi ineh 'mawang niat.' Iamo' do' neten negku Mara ngaceku ilung Mara 'mesusa' niat.' Idi Allah luk Melalud ineh pangeh nengedereh negku tu-tu.
english: Naomi said to them, “Don’t call me Naomi, which means ‘pleasant’. Instead, call me Mara, which means ‘bitter’, because God Almighty has made my life very unpleasant.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Rut ni Naomi, "Do' ui amé' lati' idi ngamung ikun luk tacin idi luk mebpeh pa puet idé luk méi' negku." Idi Naomi nengor balaneh, "Amé' mo' iko.”
english: One day Ruth said to Naomi, “Let me go to the fields and pick up the grain left behind by the workers.” Naomi replied, “Go ahead, my daughter.”

lun_bawang: Idi Boas nacing rat Baitlahim. Idi kebalaneh kuan lun luk ngeranih ineh, "Do' Tuhan ngedengan nemuyuh." Idi ideh nengor balaneh, "Do' Tuhan ngeperuan namu.”
english: Just then, Boaz arrived from Bethlehem. He greeted the men who were harvesting the grain, saying, “I want Yahweh to bless you!” They replied, “We want Yahweh to bless you, too!”

lun_bawang: Idi Boas nengitun lun dukenneh luk rayeh, "Idé luk kuan anak adi' decur ineh?”
english: Then Boaz saw Ruth, and asked the ◄foreman/man in charge of the other workmen►, “Whose daughter is that young woman?”

lun_bawang: Idi lun rayeh ineh nengor balaneh, "Ineh anak decur sakai luk nemaya' ni Naomi rat bawang Moab.
english: The foreman replied, “She is the woman from Moab who returned from there with her mother-in-law Naomi.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Boas ni Rut, "Ninger bala kini, Amu'. Aleg iko amé' ngeranih lati' dulun. Iamo' do' iko lutep ngeranih dengan lun dukenku luk decur.
english: So Boaz went over to Ruth and said to her, “Young lady, listen to me. Don’t go and pick up grain in another field. Do not go away from here. Stay here with my servant girls.

lun_bawang: Idi Rut netekeradung pa kiungneh. Idi keburi'neh ni Boas, "Ngudeh iko méi' negku, ngaceku ui ini lun sakai.”
english: When he said that, she knelt down in front of him in respect, with her face touching the ground. She exclaimed, “Why are you acting so kindly toward me, by paying attention to me? I am not even a Jew; I am a foreigner!”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Rut, "Pelaba do'mu negku. Iko pangeh nengubuk negku dengan bala luk do', sagan pana' ui na mepad kudeng lun dukenmu.”
english: She replied, “Sir, I hope you will continue to act kindly toward me. You have comforted/encouraged me, even though I am lower in status than any of your servant girls.”

lun_bawang: Idi kareb ideh kuman idi Boas nenawar neneh, "Amé' tungé' ngalap ruti ini, idi ngerereb ineh bang abpa' luk malam ni." Idi Rut netudo dengan lun luk ngeranih. Idi Boas nemaré aceh ikun luk kiriki neneh, idi Rut nekuman macing mebor. Inan teh tecehneh.
english: At mealtime, Boaz said to her, “Come over here. Take some bread and dip it in the wine vinegar and eat it.” Then when she sat down with the men who had been harvesting, he offered her some roasted grain. She ate all the grain she wanted, and had some left over.

lun_bawang: Idi kareb Rut nenalan iné' ngeranih, idi Boas nepebala nelun dukenneh, "Nima' neneh ngeranih idi ngalap sebuang ratnan luk inangel muyuh, idi aleg muyuh ngedat neneh.
english: As she stood up to start gathering grain again, Boaz ordered his workers, “Even if she gathers some grain near the bundles of grain that have been cut, do not scold her.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala ibanneh, "Nengeranih iapeh iko aco sini? Do' Allah ngeperuan lemulun luk méi' namu." Idi ieh nemada' ngadan lemulun luk inanneh ngeranih, ieh ineh Boas.
english: Her mother-in-law asked her, “Where did you gather grain today? In whose field did you work? God will surely bless the man who was kind to you.” Then Ruth told her about the man in whose field she had been working. She said, “The name of the man who owns the field where I worked today is Boaz.”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi' Rut, "Idi teh kebalaneh negku, 'Do' iko pebaya' nelun dukenku teh pad mabud lati'ku periniendeh.' “
english: Then Ruth said, “He also said to me, ‘Stay with my workers until they have finished harvesting all my grain.’”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Naomi ni Rut, "Mo, iban, do' iko pebaya' dengan lun duken i Boas, pad iko na uen lun ngedat luun lati' dulun.”
english: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it will be good for you to go to his field with his servant girls, because if you go to someone else’s field, someone might harm/molest you.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Naomi ni Rut, "O iban, do' ui nakap aceh deléi kuanmu, pad iko inan ruma'.
english: One day, Naomi said to Ruth, “My daughter, I think that I should RHQ try to arrange for you to have a husband MTY who will ◄take care of/provide for► you.

lun_bawang: Idi Rut nengor balaneh, "Amung balamu ui miak maya'.”
english: Ruth replied, “I will do everything that you have told me to do.”

lun_bawang: Idi ieh nengitun neneh, "Idé' iko ni?" Ui ini Rut, ieh ineh lun dukenmu. Ngaceku iko pupu luk muneng negku idi luk miak ngedengan negku, do' iko ngalap negku ku awanmu.”
english: He asked her, “Who are you?” She replied, “I am your servant, Ruth. Since you are the one who has a responsibility to take care of someone like me whose dead husband was your close relative, spread the corner of your cloak over my feet to show that you will marry me.”

lun_bawang: Idi Boas nengor balaneh, "O Amu, do' Tuhan ngeperuan namu. Do'mu luk nekini meluun rayeh ratnan luk atun. Na iko mili' anak adi', do' luk mula' binaweh, idi luk masi'.
english: Boaz replied, “Young lady, I hope that Yahweh will ◄bless/be kind to► you! You have acted kindly toward your mother-in-law, and now you are acting even more kindly toward me by wanting to marry me, instead of wanting to marry a young man. You have not looked for either a rich young man or a poor young man, to marry him.

lun_bawang: Idi Rut nerudap iring kukudneh macing macang. Idi ieh nekulat kareb acang dat-dat. Ngaceku kebala Boas, "Aleg nima' lun baken kali' namu iné' tungé'.”
english: So she lay at his feet until morning. But she got up and left before it was light enough that people would be able to recognize her, because Boaz said, “I do not want anyone to know that a woman was here.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Boas neneh, "Nguit kibung luk ku pakaimu ineh amé' tungé' idi malad ineh." Idi Rut nenganau' kudeng ineh. Idi Boas nengutang lélé ualuh gatang ikun luun ineh. Idi ieh nengiding neneh kuanneh. Idi Rut nuli',
english: He also said to her, “Bring to me your cloak and spread it out.” When she did that, he poured into it six measures/24 liters/50 pounds of barley, and put in on her back. Then he (OR, she) went back to the town.

lun_bawang: Idi kareb ieh nacing inan ibanneh, idi keburi' Naomi neneh, "Kudeng apeh lawému, Amu?" Idi Rut nemada' amung-amung luk inau' Boas kuanneh.
english: When Ruth arrived home, her mother-in-law asked her, “My daughter, how did ◄things go/Boaz act toward you►?” Then Ruth told her everything that Boaz had done for her and said to her.

lun_bawang: Idi teh kebalaneh, "Amung ikun ini biréneh negku teh. Ngaceku kebalaneh negku, 'Iko na miak muli' dengan na anun-anun.' “
english: She also said to Naomi, “He gave me all this barley, saying ‘I do not want you to return to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’ ”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Naomi, "O Amu, do' mulai niat, pad iko kali' anun luk miak mangun. Ngaceku Boas na miak ugka', pad ieh mangeh ratnan lawé ini aco sini."
english: Then Naomi said, “My daughter, just wait until we see what happens. I am sure that Boaz will take care of LIT the matter of your marriage today. LIT”

lun_bawang: Idi Boas iné' su luk inan pegayam munung tanga' bawang ineh, idi netudo ieneh. Idi pupu Elimalek luk muneng luk pangeh bila Boas ineh nelemba. Idi Boas nenawar, "Tungé' iko, tudo ieni." Idi ieh iné' ku tawarneh.
english: Meanwhile, Boaz went up to the town gate and sat there. That was the place where people met together to decide important matters. When the man that Boaz had mentioned came there, the close relative of Ruth and Naomi’s dead husbands who had a responsibility to take care of Naomi and Ruth, Boaz said to him, “My friend, come over here and sit down.” So the man went and sat down.

lun_bawang: Idi Boas nenawar pulu' burur lun rayeh bawang ineh, kebalaneh, "Tudo ieni." Idi ideh netudo.
english: Boaz then gathered ten of the elders of the town and asked them to sit down there also. After they sat down,

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Boas inan pupu Elimalek luk muneng ineh, "Nekini Naomi pangeh nelemubed rat Moab. Idi ieh pian masui tana' Elimalek luk pupu tau.
english: he said to the man who had the responsibility to take care of Naomi, “Naomi has returned from Moab region. She wants to sell the field that belonged to our relative Elimelech.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Boas, "Kudeng iko melih tana' ineh rat ni Naomi, idi i Rut lun Moab luk tinula' ineh mangun ku awanmu, pad tana' ineh lutep kuan inul Elimalek.”
english: Then Boaz told him, “When you buy the land from Naomi, you will also be taking Ruth, the woman who is from Moab, to be your wife, in order that she may give birth to a son who will  inherit the property of her dead husband MTY.”

lun_bawang: Idi lun ineh nengor balaneh, "Kudeng ineh peh lawéneh ruenmu, na ui pian melih tana' ineh peh, ngaceku na ui pian ngurang babaptku sebuleng. Do' iko melih tana' ineh ku libalku. Ngaceku na ui pian.”
english: Then the close relative of Ruth’s dead husband said, “If that is so, I do not want to buy the field, because then my own children would not inherit the property; Ruth’s children would inherit it. You buy the property!”

lun_bawang: Ngaceku ineh kareb lun ineh nepebala ni Boas, "Do' iko melih ineh, "Idi ieh nengelengu kasutneh, idi nemaré ineh ni Boas.
english: So that close relative said to Boaz, “You buy the field yourself!” And he took off one of his sandals and gave it to Boaz.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Boas inan amung lun rayeh idi lun mula' ineh, "Idi bang aco sini amung muyuh mangun ku lun luk nekali' ratnan ui pangeh nengalap rat ni Naomi amung-amung luk Elimalek kuan, idi amung luk Kilion idi Malun kuan.
english: Then Boaz said to the elders and all the other people who were there, “Today you have all seen that I have bought from Naomi all the property that belonged to her dead husband Elimelech and his dead sons Mahlon and Chilion.

lun_bawang: Idi kareb ineh amung lun decur nepebala ni Naomi, "Ngubur Tuhan! Ieh pangeh nemaré aceh mupun kuanmu aco sini, luk miak ngasa' namu. Merapet anak ini mebala bang bawang Israil.
english: The women of Bethlehem said to Naomi, “Praise Yahweh! Now he has given LIT you a grandson who will be the one who will have the responsibility to take care of you. We hope that he will become famous MTY throughout Israel.

lun_bawang: Idi amung decur luk bang bawang ineh nenganau' ngadan anak ineh Obed, kebaladeh, "Anak ini tinganak kuan Naomi." Idi ieh mangun ku taman Isai luk taman Daud.
english: The women who were living near her said, “It is as though Naomi now has a son!” And they named him Obed. Later, Obed became the father of Jesse, and later Jesse became the father of King David.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala awanneh Elkana, "O Hanna, ngudeh iko nangi'? Anun punmu na kuman? Anun luk inanmu dat niat? Naké ui ini meluun do' ratnan pulu' anak deléi?”
english: Then Elkanah would say to her, “Hannah, ◄why are you crying?/please quit crying!► RHQ ◄Why are you not eating?/Please eat something!► RHQ Why are you so upset/sad? You have me; is that not more important to you than if you had ten sons? (OR, I love you more than your sons would love you, even if you had ten sons.)”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Eli neneh, "Do' ugka' ngirup. Buro pad abukmu ugka'.”
english: He said to her, “How long will you continue to get drunk RHQ? ◄Throw away your wine/Quit drinking wine►!”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Hanna, "Baken kudeng ineh, Imam. Iamo' ui ini aceh decur luk mesusa' niat. Na ui nengirup. Iamo' ui pelaba susa' niat pad ui sembayang maré amung terawéku kuan Tuhan.
english: Hannah replied, “Sir, I am not drunk! I have not been drinking wine or any other alcoholic drink. I feel very distressed and I have been telling Yahweh about how I feel.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Eli neneh, "Amé' iko dengan mawang niat, idi do' Allah lun Israil maré namu anun luk pinutuhmu.”
english: Eli replied, “I wish/desire that things will go well for you. I desire that God, the one we Israeli people worship, will give you what you requested from him.”

lun_bawang: Idi keburi' Hanna, "Do' iko méi' negku." Pangeh ineh idi ieh nenalan. Idi ieh nekuman. Pangeh ineh idi na ieh mesusa' niat peh.
english: She replied, “I want you to think highly/well about me.” Then she returned to her family and after she ate something, her face no longer looked sad.

lun_bawang: pad Hanna mali'. Idi ieh nenganak aceh anak deléi luk ngadenneh Semuil. Idi kebalaneh, "Ieh luk pinutuhku ratnan Tuhan.”
english: and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, which sounds like the words in the Hebrew language that mean ‘heard by God’, because she said “Yahweh heard me when I requested from him a son.”

lun_bawang: Iamo' Hanna na iné'. Kebalaneh inan awanneh, "Kareb anak ini ugka' niti', ui sikal nguit neneh amé' pa kiung Tuhan, pad ieh tudo déi' seruked ulunneh.
english: But Hannah did not go with them. She said to her husband, “After I have weaned the baby, I will take him to Shiloh and present him to Yahweh, and he will stay there for the rest of his life.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Elkana neneh, "Nganau' anun luk do' kali'mu, pad iko pangeh niti' neneh. Iamo' nima' Tuhan ngacing jani'Neh namu." Idi decur ineh niti' anakneh pad ieh nugka' niti'.
english: Elkanah said, “Do what seems the best to you. Stay here until you have weaned him. What I desire is that Yahweh will enable you to do what you have promised.” So Hannah stayed at home and nursed her son until she weaned him.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Hanna, "Mutuh do' Imam. Ngerawé iko negku teh? Ui ini decur luk netuped ieni idi nesembayang inan Tuhan.
english: Then Hannah said to him, “Sir, ◄Do you remember me?/I solemnly affirm►, I am the woman who prayed as I stood here beside you several years ago.

lun_bawang: Idi Hanna nesembayang, kesembayangneh, "Ui mawang niat inan Tuhan, ngaceku Tuhan pangeh nengetueh negku. Idi ui meriruh nan bunu'ku, idi ui mawang niat ngaceku pedenganMu.
english: Then Hannah prayed, saying, “I rejoice in what you, Yahweh, have done. I am strong MET because I belong to you. I ◄laugh at/ridicule► my enemies, because you, Yahweh have rescued me from being taunted by them.

lun_bawang: Aleg muyuh mesido' niat, pad muyuh pebala dengan medita' niat. Ngaceku Tuhan ineh Allah luk kali', idi Ieh nutun amung kekamen lemulun.
english: You people who oppose God, stop boasting! Yahweh is a God who knows everything, and he will evaluate/judge everyone’s actions. So don’t speak so arrogantly!

lun_bawang: Idi binor lun luk metueh pinutulNeh, idi lemulun luk melaya' mangun metueh.
english: Yahweh, you break the bows/weapons of mighty soldiers, and you give strength to those who stumble because of being weak.

lun_bawang: Tuhan ineh luk ngaté idi luk ngulun; Tuhan teh luk nipa bang su luk inan até, idi luk nui teh.
english: Yahweh, you cause some people to die, and you restore some people who are almost dead. For some people, it seems that they will soon go to where the dead people are, but you cause them to become healthy again.

lun_bawang: Bunu' Tuhan miak pitayeh; Ieh melalam pa luundeh, rat i langit; Tuhan ngukum aput tana', idi maré tueh kuan Raca'Neh, idi ngerayeh Raca' luk pinili'Neh.”
english: Yahweh, you will break into pieces those who oppose you. You will cause thunder in the sky to show that you ◄oppose/are angry with► them. Yahweh, you will judge people everywhere, even those who live in the most remote places on the earth. You will give strength to the king whom you will appoint, and give him great power over his enemies.”

lun_bawang: Meluun teh kareb nateh lemak ineh ilap idi iseb, lun duken imam macing, idi pebala nan lemulun luk maré baré, "Maré sebuang uang ineh uen nadang kuan imam. Na ieh pian ku uang luk tinanek, iamo' luk mata'.”
english: Furthermore, before the fat on the meat was cut off and and burned as a sacrifice to Yahweh, the servant of the priest would sometimes come to the man who was making the sacrifice and say to him, “Give me some meat now to take to the priest for him to roast! He wants raw meat; he does not want boiled meat.”

lun_bawang: Idi Eli nengeperuan ni Elkana dengan awanneh, kebalaneh, "Do' Tuhan maré kuanmu inul ratnan decur ini, ngaceku ieh pangeh nemaré kuan Tuhan luk pangeh pinutuhneh rat Neneh." Idi didueh nuli'.
english: Then Eli would ask God to bless Elkanah and his wife, and he would say to Elkanah, “I hope/desire that Yahweh will enable your wife to give birth to other children, to take the place of the one whom she dedicated to Yahweh.” Then Elkanah and his family would return home.

lun_bawang: idi kebalaneh nedidueh, "Ngudeh medueh nganau' kekamen luk kudeng ineh? Ngaceku lun mula' ini nemada' negku ratnan kekamen medueh luk dat.
english: He said to them, “◄It is terrible that you do such things!/Why do you do such things?► RHQ Many people keep telling me about the evil things that you do.

lun_bawang: Idi seburur nabi iné' matun ni Eli dengan bala ratnan Tuhan, kebalaneh, "Kareb tepunmu Arun idi lun bang tetek ruma'neh ineh demulun raca' Masir, idi Ui nengegala' bururKu ni Arun.
english: One day, a prophet came to Eli and told him, “This is what Yahweh has told me: ‘When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I appeared to Aaron.

lun_bawang: Idi Tuhan nenawar, "Semuil! Semuil!" Idi kebala Semuil, "Anun idi, Ama'?”
english: Yahweh called, “Samuel! Samuel!” Samuel replied, “I’m here!”

lun_bawang: Idi lapung nateh nilep. Idi ieh iné' matun ni Eli, kebalaneh, "O Ama'! Iko nawar negku. Ini ui." Iamo' kebala Eli, "Na ui nenawar namu. Do' iko amé' telubid teh." Idi ieh iné' telubid.
english: Then he got up and ran to Eli. He said to him, “I am here, because you called me!” But Eli replied, “No, I did not call you. Go back to your bed.” So Samuel went and lay down again.

lun_bawang: Idi Tuhan nenawar ni Semuil teh. Idi Semuil nekulat idi iné' matun ni Eli, kebalaneh, "Anun idi, Ama'? Iko nawar negku. Ini ui." Iamo' kebala Eli, "O Asi, na ui nawar namu, lemubed iko amé' telubid teh.”
english: Then Yahweh called again, “Samuel!” So Samuel got up again and went to Eli and said, “I am here, because you called me!” But Eli said, “No, my son, I did not call you. Go back and lie down.”

lun_bawang: Idi Tuhan nenawar ni Semuil seketeluh kua'. Idi ieh iné' matun ni Eli, kebalaneh, "Anun idi Ama'? Iko nawar negku. Ini ui." Idi bang kareb ineh idi megala' kuan Eli, Tuhan luk nawar anak ineh.
english: After Samuel lay down again, Yahweh called him a third time. So again Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, “I am here, because you called me!” Then Eli realized that it was Yahweh who was calling the boy.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Eli ni Semuil, "Amé' iko telubid teh, idi kareb Ieh nawar namu teh, do' iko pebala kudeng ini, 'Do' Tuhan pebala pedingeren lun dukenMu ini.' Idi Semuil iné' telubid teh.
english: So he said to Samuel, “Go and lie down again. If someone calls you again, say ‘Speak to me, Yahweh, because I am listening!’ ” So Samuel went and lay down again.

lun_bawang: Idi Tuhan nacing idi netuped ieneh, idi nenawar neneh mepad kudeng luk atun, "Semuil! Semuil!" Idi Semuil nengor balaNeh, "Do' Tuhan pebala pedingeren lun dukenMu ini.”
english: Then Yahweh came and stood there and called as he had done the other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel said, “Speak to me, because I am listening!”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Tuhan ni Semuil, "Ui nganau' aceh kekamen luk inan megagap arang lun Israil, pad idé-idé luk ninger ineh pelaba tot.
english: Then Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen carefully. I am about to do something here in Israel that will shock/horrify IDM everyone who hears about it.

lun_bawang: Iamo' Eli nenawar ni Semuil, kebalaneh, "O anakku Semuil." Idi Semuil nengor balaneh, "Anun idi, Ama'?”
english: But Eli called him and said, “Samuel, my son!” Samuel answered, “I am here!”

lun_bawang: Idi Semuil nemada' amung bala ineh neneh. Sebila' bala pana' nateh inalumneh. Idi kebala Eli neneh, "Ieh ineh Tuhan. Nima' Neneh nganau' anun- anun luk do' pa kiungNeh.”
english: So Samuel told him everything. He did not refuse to tell him anything. Then Eli said, “He is Yahweh. I am willing for him to do what he thinks is best.”

lun_bawang: Idi udub ineh pindenger lun Pilistin, idi kebaladeh, "Udub anun luk arang baweh lun Iberani ineh?" Idi ideh kali' Pati' Pejani' Tuhan pangeh nacing su luk inan lun Iberani nelupo.
english: The Philistines asked, “What are the people in the Hebrew camp shouting about?” Someone told them that they were shouting because the chest that contained the Ten Commandments of Yahweh had been brought to them.

lun_bawang: Ideh matot, kebaladeh, "Tuhan pangeh nacing arang baweh ineh. Mesusa' kuan tau! Ngaceku nateh luk mangun kudeng ini atun!
english: Then the Philistines became very afraid. They said, “One of the Israelis’ gods has come into their camp to help them We are in big trouble now! Nothing like this has happened to us before!

lun_bawang: Arod ineh pindenger Eli, idi kebalaneh, "Anunké ria' ineh?" Idi dengan mesaget ideh nacing iné' mada' bala ineh ni Eli.
english: Eli asked, “Why are they making all that noise?” The messenger ran over to Eli and told him the news.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala lun Beniamin ineh ni Eli, "Ui ini nacing rat nepebunu'. Idi aco sini teh ui pangeh neburo rat arang baweh." Idi kebala Eli, "O Asi, kudeng apehké ayu déi'?”
english: The messenger said to Eli, “I have just come from where the armies were fighting. I left there earlier today.” Eli asked, “What happened?”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala lun Beniamin ineh, "Lun Israil pangeh neburo rat pa kiung lun Pilistin. Idi mula' tu-tu lun Israil pangeh naté. Meluun teh dueh anakmu, Hopni idi Pinihas teh pangeh naté. Idi Pati' Pejani' Allah pana' pangeh inaro bunu' ineh.”
english: The man replied, “The Philistines defeated our Israeli army. They killed thousands of our soldiers, and the others ran away. The Philistines killed your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. They also captured God’s sacred chest.”

lun_bawang: Idi kareb ieh lélé maté kebala amung decur luk nengimet neneh, "Aleg iko merapang ngaceku iko nenganak aceh anak deléi." Iamo' na ieh neninger idi nengor baladeh.
english: The women who were helping her tried to encourage her by saying to her, “You have given birth to a son!” But she did not pay any attention DOU to what they said.

lun_bawang: Iamo' ieh neneten anak ineh Ikabod, kebalaneh, "Ubur lun Israil pangeh neburo!" Ngaceku Pati' Pejani' Allah pangeh inaro, idi ngaceku ibanneh idi awanneh teh pangeh naté.
english: She named the boy Ichabod, which means ‘no glory’, because she said, “God’s glory has departed from Israel.” She said that because God’s sacred chest had been captured and because her husband and her father-in-law had died.

lun_bawang: Idi teh ieh nepebala, "Ubur lun Israil pangeh neburo, ngaceku Pati' Pejani' Allah pangeh inaro."
english: She said, “God’s glory has left Israel, because God’s sacred chest has been captured!” And then she died.

lun_bawang: Kareb lun Asdod nekali' dereh luk kudeng ineh, idi kebaladeh, "Aleg Pati' Pejani' tudo arang tau, ngaceku Allah lun Israil ngukum netau idi Dagon akang tau pana'.”
english: The men of Ashdod realized why this was happening, and they cried out, “The god of the Israeli people is punishing us and is also punishing our god Dagon. So we cannot allow the sacred chest of the god of the Israelis to remain here!”

lun_bawang: Idi ideh nemubuh Pati' Pejani' ineh iné' déi' Ekron. Iamo' kareb ieh nacing déi', idi lun bang bawang ineh nengitang, kebaladeh, "Ideh nenguit Pati' Pejani' Allah lun Israil ineh amé' netau, pad tau maté.”
english: So they took the sacred chest to Ekron city. But when the men carried the sacred chest into Ekron, the people there cried out, “Why are you bringing the sacred chest of the God of the Israelis into our city RHQ? By doing that you will cause us and the rest of our people to die!”

lun_bawang: Idi lun rayeh-rayeh nenawar amung imam, idi lun luk mileh mangun, kebaladeh, "Kudeng apehké kai ku Pati' Pejani' Tuhan ineh. Anunké luk barén kai maya' ineh lemubed amé' su iratneh.”
english: Then they summoned their priests and their ◄diviners/men who practice rituals to find out what would happen in the future►. They asked them, “What should we do with the sacred chest of Yahweh? Tell us how we should send it back to its own land.”

lun_bawang: Idi nekini do' nganau' aceh keréta luk mebaruh idi ngalap dueh sapi' tineh luk niti' anak, idi luk na pekalai nan nengacang paga'. Nganau' sapi' ineh nan keréta ineh, idi nguit anak didueh lemubed rat i puet didueh amé' bang libung.
english: “So you must build a new cart. Then get two cows that have very recently given birth to calves. They must be cows that have never been hitched to a cart MTY. Hitch those cows to the new cart, and take the calves away from their mothers.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala lun Bait Semes, "Idé miak tuped pa kiung Tuhan Allah luk Meligan ini? Idi idéké miak inan tau maré Pati' Pejani' ini, pad tau mepuit rat Neneh?”
english: They sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-Jearim city to tell them, “The people of Philistia have returned Yahweh’s sacred chest to us! Come here and take it away!”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Semuil, "Mungen muyuh amung lun Israil déi' Mispa. Ui sikal sembayang kuan muyuh inan Tuhan.”
english: Then Samuel told them, “All you Israeli people must gather with me at Mizpah. Then I will pray to Yahweh for you.”

lun_bawang: Idi ideh netebubpun déi' Mispa. Idi ideh nengook abpa'. Idi inisakdeh pa kiung Tuhan. Idi kareb aco sineh teh ideh mawa', kebaladeh, "Kai pangeh mesala' inan Tuhan." Idi Semuil tudo déi' Mispa idi nengimet nelun Israil.
english: So they gathered at Mizpah, which was the town where Samuel previously was the leader of the Israeli people. They had a big ceremony there. They drew water from a well, and poured the water on the ground while Yahweh watched. To show that they were sorry for having worshiped idols, they did not eat any food on that day, and they confessed that they had sinned against Yahweh.

lun_bawang: Kebaladeh ni Semuil, "Aleg iko ugka' sembayang inan Tuhan Allah tau pad Ieh muit netau rat bang palad lun Pilistin.”
english: They told Samuel, “Pray to Yahweh to rescue us from the Philistia army MTY, and do not stop pleading!”

lun_bawang: Idi Semuil nengalap aceh batu. Idi ieh nenaped ineh arang Mispa dengan Sen. Idi ieh neneten batu ineh "Batu Pedengan", kebalaneh, "Macing ieni Tuhan pangeh nengedengan netau.”
english: After that happened, Samuel took a large stone and set it up between Mizpah and Jeshanah towns. He named the stone ‘Ebenezer’, which means ‘stone of help’, because he said “Yahweh has helped us until the present time.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebaladeh neneh, "Iko pangeh mengered. Idi anakmu ineh na maya' lawému. Ngaceku ineh do' iko ngikit aceh raca' kuan kai, pelé ieh miak ngimet nekai mepad kudeng amung pupu baken.”
english: They said to him, “Listen! You are now old, and your sons are not like you. Appoint a king to rule over us, like the kings that other countries have!”

lun_bawang: Idi Semuil dat niat ku baladeh mutuh raca'. Idi ieh nesembayang inan Tuhan.
english: Samuel was very unhappy with them for requesting that, so he prayed to Yahweh about it.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Tuhan, "Do' ninger bala pupu ini namu. Ngaceku baken iko luk tila'deh. Iamo' ideh nenecan Negku, pele' Ui na mangun ku raca'deh.
english: Yahweh replied, “Do what they have requested you to do. But ◄do not think/the truth is not► that you are the one whom they are really rejecting. I have been their king, and I am the one they are really rejecting.

lun_bawang: Idi lun mula' na sikal ninger bala Semuil. Iamo' kebaladeh, "Aganeh kai aceh raca'.
english: But the people refused to pay attention to what Samuel said. They said, “We do not care what you say! We want a king!

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Tuhan ni Semuil, "Ninger iko baladeh, idi ngikit aceh raca' kuandeh." Idi Semuil nengecuk nelun Israil muli'.
english: Yahweh replied, “Do what they are telling you to do. Give them a king!” So Samuel agreed, and then he sent the people home.

lun_bawang: Idi tuda'-tuda keladai Kis pangeh neraruh. Idi kebala Kis ni Saul, "Do' iko nguit seburur lun duken maya' namu amé' nakap keladai ineh.”
english: One day, some of Kish’s female donkeys wandered off. So Kish told Saul, “Take one of my servants with you, and go and search for the donkeys!”

lun_bawang: Kareb didueh nacing déi' bawang Sup, idi kebala Saul nelun dukenneh luk maya' neneh, "Do' kita muli', ngaceku napeh i Ama' ugka' ngerawé keladai ineh idi ngimun ngerawé nekiteh.”
english: Finally, they came to the area of Zuph. Then Saul said to the servant, “Let’s go back home. If we do not do that, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.”

lun_bawang: Kebala lun duken ineh, "Ui inan aceh balad pirak luk isuut barénku neneh, pad ieh mada' nekiteh su apeh luk inan nakap nedeh.”
english: The servant replied, “Look at this! I have a small silver coin. I can give this to him, and then he will tell us where to go to find the donkeys.”

lun_bawang: -11Idi kebala Saul, "Matu bala mini. Do' kiteh amé'." Idi didueh iné' bawang su luk inan nabi Allah ineh. Idi laba' didueh mudik irang amé' matun bawang ineh, didueh nepapu' tuda'-tuda' anak adi' decur luk amé' ngereb abpa'. Idi didueh nengitun nedeh, "Inanké lun nier ieni?" (Mon lawé arang lun Israil kareb lun amé' ngitun Allah, kebaladeh, "Amé' tau matun nelun luk nier," ngaceku kareb ineh, lun luk titen nabi nekini, ieh ineh titen lun luk nier.)
english: Saul said, “Okay, let’s go talk to him.” So they went to the town where the prophet lived. As they were going up the hill into the town, they met some young women who were coming out of the town to get some water from a well. One of them asked the women, “Is the seer in the town today?” They said that because previously, if people in Israel wanted a message from God, they would say, “Let’s go to the seer,” and people who now are called prophets were at that time called ‘those who see ◄visions from God/all that God sees►.’

lun_bawang: Idi kebaladeh ineh, "Inan. Siruh, idi ieh pa atun medueh. Do' medueh mesaget. Ngaceku aco sini teh ieh nacing bang bawang ini, ngaceku lun mula' maré baré luun bubpun luun surud ineh.
english: So Saul and the servant entered the town. As they went through the gates, they saw Samuel as he was coming toward them, on the way to where people were going to offer sacrifices.

lun_bawang: Kareb Semuil nenier ni Saul, idi bala Tuhan nacing neneh, "Ini lun luk pangeh bida'Ku namu! Ieh luk miak ngimet pupuKu.”
english: Samuel replied, “I am that man. Go ahead of me with your servant to the place where the people make sacrifices. Both of you will eat with me today. Tomorrow morning I will tell you what you are wanting to know, and then I will send you home.

lun_bawang: Idi Saul iné' matun ni Semuil munung tanga' bawang, kebalaneh, "Mada' kuanku iapeh ruma' lun luk nier ineh?”
english: Also, do not worry any more about those donkeys that wandered away three days ago. ◄Someone has found them/They have been found►. But what you need to know is that it is you and your family that all the Israeli people are wanting!” RHQ

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Saul, "Ui ini lun inul Beniamin luk meluun pawa' arang lun Israil? Idi tetek ruma'ku pana' luk meluun dat arang lun Beniamin. Kudeng apehké iko pebala negku kudeng ineh?”
english: Then Samuel told the cook, “Bring to me the special piece of meat that I told you to set aside.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Semuil nelun luk ngelak, "Nguit babpat luk pangeh bida'ku namu, 'Rangenmu ieh setau'.' “
english: After they finished eating, they returned to the town. Then Samuel took Saul up to the flat roof of his house, and fixed a bed for him.

lun_bawang: Idi Semuil nengalap aceh seréi' umau, idi ieh nengutang umau ineh luun uluh Saul. Idi ieh nemuen neneh, kebalaneh, "Naké Tuhan pangeh nengumau namu pad iko mangun ku raca' lun Israil? Iko miak ngimet pupu Tuhan. Idi iko miak muit nedeh rat bang palad bunu' pekelibut. Idi ini mangun ku tanu' kuanmu, idi Tuhan pangeh nengumau namu mangun ku raca' amung babpatNeh.
english: Then Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured some of it on Saul’s head. Then he kissed Saul on the cheek, and told him, “I am doing this because Yahweh has chosen you to be the leader of his Israeli people.

lun_bawang: Idi amung lemulun luk pekalai neneh mawa nier neneh nganau' kudeng ineh. Idi ideh nepebala seburur dengan seburur, "Anunké luk pangeh mangun kuan anak Kis ineh? Matuké i Saul pana' arang lun nabi?”
english: When people who had known Saul previously heard him speaking messages from God as the prophets were doing, they said to each other, “What has happened to this son of Kish? Is he now really one of the ◄prophets/men who speak messages from God►?”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala seburur rat bang bawang ineh, "Idéké tamandeh?" Idi ideh ineh mangun ku aceh bala, "Matuké i Saul pana' arang lun nabi?”
english: One of the men who lived there replied, “Saul cannot be a prophet, because all prophets receive their power to speak messages from God, not from their parents.” And that is why, when people hear about a report of someone prophesying, they think about what happened to Saul and say, “We are surprised about that person becoming a prophet, like we were surprised to hear that Saul had really become one of the prophets.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala taman pinaken Saul neneh idi nelun dukenneh ineh, "Iné' iapeh medueh?" Idi kebala Saul, "Kai iné' nakap keladai ineh. Kareb kai nenier na ideh idi, idi kai iné' matun ni Semuil.”
english: Later, Saul’s uncle saw him there, and asked him, “Where did you go?” Saul replied, “We went to look for the donkeys. When we could not find them, we came here to ask Samuel if he could tell us where they were.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala taman pinaken Saul, "Anun bala Semuil nemedueh?”
english: Saul’s uncle replied, “What did Samuel tell you?”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Saul kuan taman pinakenneh, "Ieh nemada' nekai matu keladai ineh pangeh ilap." Iamo' ratnan mangun ku raca' luk pangeh bida' Semuil ineh, na ieh nemada' ineh neneh.
english: Saul replied, “He assured us that the donkeys had been found.” But he did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about him becoming the king of Israel.

lun_bawang: Idi ideh nengitun Tuhan teh, "Tungé'ké léi sineh?" Idi Tuhan nengor baladeh, "Ieh sigapung arang amung repapeh.”
english: So they asked Yahweh, “Where is Saul?” Yahweh replied, “He is hiding among the army equipment.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Semuil kuan lun mula' ineh, "Nier muyuh lun luk pangeh pinili' Tuhan. Ngaceku seburur pana' nateh luk mepad kudeng ieh." Idi lun mula' ineh nengudub, "Mipu ulun raca'!”
english: Then Samuel said to all the people there, “This is the man whom Yahweh has chosen to be your king. Among all us Israeli people, there is no one like him!” Then all the people shouted, “We hope that this king will live a long time!”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala tuda'-tuda' lun luk dat, "Kudeng apeh lemulun ini miak muit netau?" Idi ideh nenecan neneh idi na nemaré baré kuanneh. Iamo' i Saul sibengel.
english: But some worthless men said, “◄How can this man save us from our enemies?/This man will not be able to save us from our enemies.►” RHQ They despised him, and refused to give him any gifts to show that they would be loyal to him. But Saul did not say anything to rebuke them.

lun_bawang: Idi Nahas lun Amon iné' nengelibut bawang Yabis Giliad. Idi kebala amung lun bang bawang Yabis ineh ni Nahas, "Do' iko pejani' nekai, idi kai mangun ku lun dukenmu.”
english: About a month later, King Nahash of Ammon led his army across the Jordan River, and they surrounded Jabesh city in the Gilead region. But all the men of Jabesh went and said to Nahash, “Make an agreement/treaty with us not to kill us, and then we will let you rule us.”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Nahas nedeh, "Ui pian pejani' nemuyuh dengan sebuleng ukum. Mateh muyuh pa tinueh tekulanku pelé lun Israil uen ngigu'.”
english: Nahash replied, “I will do that if you do one thing. Allow us to gouge out all the right eyes of your people. By doing that we will cause the people in other countries to despise all you Israeli people.”

lun_bawang: Kebala amung lun rayeh Yabis neneh, "Nima' nekai tudu' aco kinioneh, pelé kai ngecuk nelun duken amé' bang amung babpat lun Israil. Kudeng ayuneh seburur pana' nateh luk muit nekai, idi kai miak maré burur kai namu.”
english: The leaders of Jabesh replied, “Do not attack us for the next seven days. During that time, we will send messengers throughout Israel to tell them what you are demanding. If no one will help us, then we will ◄surrender to you/allow you to do to us whatever you want►.”

lun_bawang: Idi Saul muli' pebaya' dengan sapi'neh. Idi kebalaneh, "Anun susa' lun mula' ineh, pad ideh nangi'?" Idi ideh nemada' neneh amung bala lun Yabis ineh.
english: At that time, Saul was plowing in the field. When he returned home, he asked, “Why are all the people crying?” So they told him what the messengers from Jabesh had reported.

lun_bawang: Idi kebaladeh nelun luk icuk luk pangeh nacing ineh, "Do' muyuh mada' pupu muyuh, pekak nebpa kareb pun mét idang muyuh miak uen ngedengan." Kareb lun Yabis neninger bala ineh, idi ideh pelaba awang niat.
english: So Saul sent messengers back to the people at Jabesh to tell them, “We will rescue/save you by noontime tomorrow.” When the people of Jabesh heard that message, they were very joyful/happy.

lun_bawang: Idi kebaladeh ni Nahas, "Pekak nebpa kai miak remuat amé' matun nemuyuh. Miak muyuh nganau' kuan kai anun luk do' bang terawé muyuh.”
english: Then the men of Jabesh told Nahash, “Tomorrow we will surrender to you, and then you can do to us whatever you want to.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala lun mula' ineh ni Semuil, "Idé' luk nepebala, 'Miakké i Saul ngimet netau?' Nguit lemulun ineh amé' tungé' pad kai ngaté nedeh.”
english: Then the people of Jabesh said to Samuel, “Where are those men who said that they did not want Saul to be our king? Bring them here, and we will kill them!”

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Saul, "Aco sini seburur pana' nateh miak pitayen. Ngaceku aco sini teh Tuhan pangeh nemuit nelun Israil.”
english: But Saul replied, “No, we are not going to execute anyone today, because this is the day that Yahweh has saved us Israeli people. It is a day to rejoice, not to kill anyone.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Semuil nelun mula' ineh, "Do' tau amé' déi' Gilgal idi ngeletep baruh imet raca' déi'.”
english: Then Samuel said to the people, “Let’s all go to Gilgal, and there we will again proclaim that Saul is our king.”

lun_bawang: Kebala Semuil nelun Israil, "Ui pangeh neninger putuh muyuh. Idi ui pangeh nengikit seburur mangun ku raca' muyuh.
english: Then Samuel said this to all the Israeli people: “I have done everything that you told me to do, and I have given/appointed a king to rule you.

lun_bawang: Idi lun mula' ineh nengor balaneh, "Na iko nenaluk nekai. Idi na iko nengedereh nekai. Na iko nengalap aceh anun-anun rat bang palad seburur pana'.”
english: They replied, “No, you have never cheated anyone or oppressed anyone or accepted a bribe from anyone.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Semuil, "Aco sini Tuhan idi raca' luk pinili'Neh mangun ku lun nekali' kuan amung muyuh, idi muyuh kali' ui na mesala'." Idi kebala lun mula' ineh, "Tuhan ineh mangun ku Lun luk Nekali'.”
english: Then Samuel said, “Today Yahweh can testify, and the king whom you chose can testify, that I have not taken a bribe from anyone.” They replied, “Yes, Yahweh can say that he knows that is true.”

lun_bawang: Idi teh kebala Semuil, "Tuhan ineh luk nemili' ni Musa idi i Arun, idi luk nenguit amung tepun muyuh remuat rat bang bawang Masir.
english: Samuel continued by saying, “Yahweh is the one who appointed Moses and Aaron to lead our ancestors. He is the one who brought them out of Egypt. And he is the one who will testify that what I am saying is true.

lun_bawang: Kareb Yakub dengan amung uang tetek ruma'neh iné' déi' Masir idi lun Masir nengedereh nedeh, idi tepun muyuh nengitang mutuh pedengan ratnan Tuhan pad Ieh nengecuk ni Musa idi Arun luk nenguit nedeh remuat rat bang bawang Masir, pad ideh tudo bang bawang ini.
english: “Many years after Jacob went to Egypt, our ancestors pleaded to Yahweh to help them. So Yahweh sent Moses and Aaron to them, and they led our ancestors out of Egypt, and eventually they settled in this land.

lun_bawang: Idi kareb muyuh nenier ni Nahas, raca' lun Amon macing pebunu' nemuyuh, idi muyuh na pian ku Tuhan mangun ku raca' muyuh. Kebala muyuh, 'Do' aceh raca' ngimet nekai.'
english: “But now, when king Nahash of Ammon came with his army to attack you, you were afraid. So, you came to me, and said, ‘We want a king to rule us,’ even though Yahweh was already your king!

lun_bawang: Ngaceku ineh do' muyuh tuped ieni. Nier muyuh tanu' luk rayeh luk ruen Tuhan pa kiung muyuh.
english: “Now stand here quietly and see the great thing that Yahweh is about to do.

lun_bawang: idi kebaladeh ni Semuil, "Sembayang iko mutuh inan Tuhan Allahmu kuan kai ini, pelé kai na maté. Ngaceku kai pangeh nengula' sala' ineh ku kai nemutuh aceh raca'.”
english: They cried out to Samuel, “Pray for us! We have added to our previous sins by requesting a king! Pray to Yahweh, your God, in order that we will not die because of having done that!”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Semuil, "Aleg muyuh matot. Sagan tu pana' muyuh pangeh nenganau' amung kekamen luk dat ini, aleg muyuh lemubed ratnan Tuhan. Iamo' do' muyuh sembayang nan Tuhan dengan amung niat muyuh.
english: Samuel replied, “Do not be afraid! You have done this evil thing, but do not turn away from doing the things that Yahweh wants you to do. Instead, serve Yahweh wholeheartedly.

lun_bawang: Idi Yonatan nengelaya' baweh lun Pilistin luk déi' Giba. Idi lun Pilistin nekali' bala ineh, idi Saul nengiup serupit bang anid babpat bawang, pad nawar nelun Iberani amé' pebunu'.
english: Jonathan and the men who were with him attacked the Philistine soldiers who were camped at Geba. The other Philistines heard about that. So Saul realized that the army of Philistia would probably come to fight the Israelis again. So Saul sent messengers to blow trumpets throughout Israel to gather the people together and proclaim to them, “All you Hebrews need to hear that now the Philistines will start a war with us!”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Saul, "Maré kuanku baré sabpen, idi baré luk nguit pedo'." Idi ieh nemaré baré sabpen ineh.
english: So Saul said to the soldiers, “Bring to me an animal to be completely burned on the altar and one for the offering to enable us to maintain fellowship with God.” So the men did that.

lun_bawang: Iamo' kebala Semuil, "Anun kekamenmu ineh?" Kebala Saul, "Ngaceku ui nenier nelun mula' ineh nepatad rat negku, idi iko pana' nateh nacing kareb aco luk bida'mu ineh. Idi teh amung lun Pilistin nepamung dé'i Mikmas.
english: Samuel saw what Saul had done, and he said to Saul, “Why have you done this?” Saul replied, “I saw that my men were leaving me and running away, and that you did not come here during the time that you said that you would come, and that the Philistine army was gathering together at Micmash.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Semuil, "Kekamenmu ini mebacé. Na iko nemaya' bala Tuhan Allahmu namu. Kudeng iko nemaya' balaNeh, kali' rungen Ieh ngeletep imetmu pa luun lun Israil macing ruked-ruked.
english: Samuel replied, “What you did was very foolish! You have not obeyed what Yahweh, your God, commanded about sacrifices. If you had obeyed him, God would have allowed you and your descendants to rule Israel for a long time.

lun_bawang: Idi seburur lun mileh nuno pana' nateh nekali' bang aput bawang Israil. Ngaceku lun Iberani bibpeng lun Pilistin, na miak nganau' pelapet idi gaman.
english: At that time, there were no men in Israel who ◄were blacksmiths/could make things from iron►. The people of Philistia would not permit the Israelis to do that, because they were afraid that they would make iron swords and spears for the Hebrews to fight with.

lun_bawang: Idi kebala anak adi' ineh, "Do' nganau' luk pianmu. Ui idi denganmu.”
english: The young man who was carrying Jonathan’s weapons said, “Do what you think is the best thing for us to do. I will help you.”

lun_bawang: Idi kebala Yonatan, "Do' kiteh amé' silagan sirendeh.
english: Then Jonathan said, “Okay, come with me. We will cross the valley to where the Philistia army is, and allow them to see us.

lun_bawang: Idi didueh nesilagan nelun Pilistin. Idi kebala lun Pilistin, "Siruh! Lun Iberani ineh pangeh neremuat rat bang batu su luk inandeh nesigapung.”
english: When the two of them crossed the valley, the Philistia soldiers saw them coming. They said, “Look! The Hebrews are crawling out of the holes in which they have been hiding!”
